Changelog

0.30

  • One track's loops along the scale: hold SHIFT, hold a track's button, press OCT+ or OCT−: that track's loops and overdubs move a step of the scale, the others not (TRANSP T3 +2), on top of the move of all the loops. An overdub made meanwhile plays as played; sessions and copies keep it; emptying the track resets it.
  • The keys move with the loops: on a track, the white keys play the scale moved as far as that track's loops (all the loops' move and its own), so new material and overdubs fit what is there.
  • SHIFT no longer shows the audio's load.
  • FM's macros heard: BRIGHTNESS (was BRIGHT) moves the modulators about 27 dB either way and the feedback with them; DETUNE pulls the carriers ±40 cents apart and the modulators ±25 cents off them, so even a patch of one carrier beats and roughens. Every macro, on every engine, answers early in its turn: a quarter of the way gives half the change.
  • Macros named for what they do: FM BRIGHTNESS, DETUNE or INHARMONIC (was SKEW), SATURATION (was GRIT), MOTION; ANIMA NOISE (was AIR), FORMANT (was VOWEL), RESONATOR (was SPACE); CALIGULA WAVEFORM (was EDGE), MOD DEPTH (was DEPTH), FEEDBACK (was CHAOS), DELAY (was ECHO), TOUCHES (was HAND), GATE RATE (was PULSE); RUSSOLO RANDOMNESS (was CHAOS). A long name takes a smaller size on the dial.

0.29

  • ANIMA, a lo-fi engine: its voices are computed at half the sample rate (22.05 kHz: nothing above 11 kHz) and drawn out to the full rate by straight lines; pitches, rates and filters scaled to stay where they were. It costs the chip about 9 % of its time a voice instead of 15 %.
  • Eight new ANIMA kinds (generation 3): PLUCK, REED, FOG, ORGAN, BITS, DRIFT, MURMUR, HOWL; and every kind draws wider: any waveform, wider intervals and ratios, detuning, plucked or swelling envelopes, other gestures, pulsing tremolos, crushed rates, sharp resonances.
  • Five new FM families (generation 3): PLUCK (strings, bright or dark), MALLET (marimba, vibraphone, kalimba), and the stranger WARP, GLITCH and RUBBER; any family may now come out plucked, with a modulator on another ratio or an operator detuned.
  • ANIMA's macros heard: TONE four octaves either way (and the FM's brightness), the kind's macro from nothing to far more (DRIVE down: a pure tone), SPACE from dry to a long ring, MOTION from a still hand to a quick one with a tremolo; and each answers early in its turn.
  • ANIMA lighter still: the wavetables its voices play are copied into RAM while they play (from the flash a read could cost twenty times as much). To make room, a track's loops now hold about 500 notes between them (were about 1000); a session saved with more loads the first 500 or so of each track.
  • Sounds saved before (sessions, presets) are drawn again exactly as they were — the new kinds and families are generation 3's — though an ANIMA sound now plays at the lower rate.

0.28

  • Copy a track onto another: hold a track's button (0.8 s) to copy it — COPIED, its button blinking — then hold another track's button to paste it there — PASTED. The tone (engine, the four sounds and their macros, filter, granulator, crush, send, octave, path) and all the loops go across; level and pan stay. The next hold copies again.
  • Tracks: what the manual called layers are now called tracks, everywhere.

0.27

  • Loops moved along the scale: SHIFT + OCT+ / OCT− moves every loop of every track one step of the chosen scale up or down (C to D in C major), the notes sounding moving at once; up to two octaves of the scale either way, shown on the screen. Another scale or root chosen meanwhile is walked instead. An overdub recorded while the loops are moved plays back as played. Sessions keep it; sessions saved before load as they were. The screen says TRANSP +2, TRANSP 0.
  • An empty session is a clean slate: choosing an empty slot on the SESSIONS page now starts afresh, as at switching on — no loops, no latches, new sounds on every track, every setting, the scale, the reverb and the transposition at their defaults. The session you were in stays saved as it was.
  • Drones stay whole in loops: a note still held when REC closes the loop is tied over the loop's end, sounding on as it goes round instead of being let go and struck again each time (which was heard as a stutter, ANIMA and CALIGULA above all).
  • No click when ANIMA reuses a voice: a voice taken over for a new note (loops going round, many notes at once) kept its comb resonator, phaser and sample hold from the note before, heard again at full level as the new note began. They now start empty.
  • No more bursts when a loop starts: with the machine busy (many release tails ringing), a loop starting — CALIGULA above all — could make the audio late for a few milliseconds, heard as a burst. Tonitor now measures what each voice and organism costs as it plays, and before anything new starts it makes room ahead, letting the oldest release tails go quickly, so the audio is never late. A held note is let go only if the audio is late after all (past 100 %). SHIFT shows the load now, as one percentage.

0.26

  • RUSSOLO, a fourth engine: noise, logic and broken buffers, re-making the techniques of Robert Heel's Noisferatu. Seventeen kinds — HOLD, DUST, GATES, CRACKLE (noise); NOR, XOR, RING, CASCADE, CLANG (oscillators combined bit by bit); CHUNKS, JUMP, WANDER, BEND, QUAD (generated buffers read with their addresses bent); BLIPS, WALK, CHORD (chance-driven tones) — at a third of the sample rate in 10 bits, crushed and sample-held further as each sound says. A key gates it and sets its pitch; one organism a track, as CALIGULA. Its macros: the kind's two parameters, CRUSH and CHAOS. The paths lean it: AMBIENT to chords, dust, crackle, blips and walks, clean and slow; EXPERIMENTAL to logic and bent buffers, crushed and abrupt. Presets: 64 for it too.
  • Sessions are a fuller snapshot: they now also keep each track's granulator character and its latched notes (which sound again on load). The master reverb was already kept. Sessions and presets saved before load as they were.

0.25

  • Voices from a shared pool: twelve voices for all the tracks instead of two fixed per track. A track takes as many as its notes need — a twelve-note chord on one track, single notes on others. With all twelve busy, a new note takes the oldest release (any track), else its own track's oldest held note, else the oldest held anywhere.

0.24

  • Sessions are written to and read from the flash a sector at a time: about 50 KB of RAM freed (more than half of it), for more voices and a fourth engine to come. Nothing changes in use; every session saved before loads.
  • The start-up screen's name fits the screen.

0.23

  • Overdubs in and out: hold PLAY and the chosen track's loops appear on the white keys (the first loop on the leftmost, then each overdub), lit while they play and shown on the screen. A key takes its loop out or brings it back in — while they play, at once and from its start; while stopped, choosing what PLAY will start. PLAY pressed and let go still starts and stops the loops. Sessions keep which loops are out.

0.22

  • Macros: the black key before SHIFT turns EDIT on (lit) and off. While it is on, KNOB 1–4 are four macros that reshape the chosen track's sound live, chosen for each engine and kind of sound — FM: BRIGHT, DETUNE or SKEW, GRIT, MOTION; ANIMA: TONE, GRAINS / AIR / FM / VOWEL / DRIVE, SPACE, MOTION; CALIGULA: EDGE, DEPTH, CHAOS or ECHO, HAND or PULSE. The middle is the sound as drawn. Sessions and presets keep them; HOME starts a new sound in the middle.
  • FM in tune: a slip in the FM generator put nearly every operator ratio near an even multiple, so patches played about two octaves above the key and lost most of their designed ratios (bells, near-harmonic beating). New sounds now have the ratios they were designed with, at the key's pitch. Sounds saved before (sessions, presets) come back exactly as they were.

0.21

  • Presets: SHIFT + SAVE opens the chosen track's engine's presets, 64 an engine (P1–P64), four a page. SAVE held saves the track's sound into the slot chosen (asking OVERWRITE? over a full one), SAVE loads it.
  • Richer, smarter generators (generation 1):
    • FM: eight new families — CHOIR, BOWED, HOLLOW, BLOOM, TIDE, SHARDS, STATIC, WIND; every patch shaped with care (no screaming sidebands, brightness scaled down the keyboard), gentler mutations, and several patches drawn and measured, keeping one whose brightness suits the path.
    • ANIMA: six new kinds — TIDE, CHOIR, SHARDS, BOWL, DUST, MACHINE; the filter follows the keyboard; the second oscillator's interval suits the path; AMBIENT sounds get a space to ring in.
    • CALIGULA: four new species — LITANY, UNDERTOW, WIRE, MOTH; four new tunings (fourths, a minor seventh, open fifths, a quarter-tone cluster); the hand plays phrases, often on a pulse; a bed that the gates never close.
  • Sounds saved before (in sessions) come back exactly as they were: the older generators are kept as they were, and a test checks it.

0.20 — Tonitor

  • The firmware is now called Tonitor (it was developed as ACOUSMA). The FM-1 shows the new name at start-up and over USB ("FM-1 Tonitor"); sessions saved before keep working.
  • A browser installer: install from Chrome, Edge or Opera over Web MIDI, no tools needed.
  • The website, the logo, the manual online.

0.19

  • SHIFT + PLAY with no loop playing starts every loop there is, all together from their starts.

0.18

  • On the SESSIONS page, SAVE held saves into the slot shown: an empty one asks SAVE NEW, a full one asks OVERWRITE? (on NO until turned to YES).
  • Slots holding a session show their number in red; empty slots in grey with EMPTY.

0.17

  • ANIMA EXPERIMENTAL made much wilder and more textured: crushed rates, folding, dragged noise, scattered grains, fast tremolo, a ringing comb.
  • SHIFT + PLAY stops every loop on every track, from any track.
  • The level meter runs across the bottom of the screen, above the pan; the level is shown in %.
  • Long messages (EXPERIMENTAL) fit the screen.

0.16

  • Generative paths: AMBIENT and EXPERIMENTAL on the two leftmost black keys, per track, for every engine.
  • CALIGULA's slow swells and long releases now play as designed.
  • Under heavy load the note just played is never the one dropped (ANIMA notes no longer go silent beside CALIGULA); SHIFT shows the audio load.

0.15

  • Latching: hold keys, then press SHIFT. On the SCALE page SELECT chooses the root, ALGORITHM the scale.

0.14

  • SHIFT (the rightmost black key) and latched keys.

0.13

  • CALIGULA played from the keys like the other engines, a simulated hand on its plates.

0.12

  • CALIGULA, a third engine.

0.1 – 0.11

  • FM and ANIMA engines; six tracks with two voices each; a free looper per track, then up to ten overdubs; track level, pan and reverb send; the master reverb; 64 session slots; scales on the white keys; the DJ filter, the granulator and the crush per track.
